author: Codex assessment agent /root/liberal_conservative (AI-assisted doctrinal interpretation)
changeNote: Completed 240 independently considered answers to the current bank from the scoped doctrine. No imported 12Axes vectors or score targets. User authorised neutral answers and completion on 2026-10-04. Conditional modern applications and mixed-causation modelling are explicitly inferred, not claims of direct statements or scientific findings. Independent review completed on 2026-10-04; question-meaning and evidence corrections are recorded in review notes.

metadata.name: Conservative Centrism
metadata.description: Moderate parliamentary conservatism in the One Nation tradition, combining established institutions, a mixed economy and social obligations. The Tory Reform Group provides a starting point, not evidence for every contemporary conservative.
metadata.period: British One Nation and Middle Way tradition, post-1945
metadata.scope: Moderate parliamentary conservatism in the One Nation tradition, combining established institutions, a mixed economy and social obligations. The Tory Reform Group provides a starting point, not evidence for every contemporary conservative. This is a representative interpretation of the specified doctrine, not answers personally submitted by every adherent. Modern technological questions apply the doctrine conditionally. Trait-specific neutral responses express a stated mixed-causation model where the doctrine rejects a single fixed causal priority; they are not empirical scientific estimates.
metadata.phrase: A society preserving constitutional institutions while using gradual reform and social protection to maintain cohesion.

sources.title: TRG One Nation Day: Siobhan Aarons opening speech
Right to buy: Past, present and future

axes.brief: One Nation parliamentary conservatism accepts electoral competition, legal restraints and gradual constitutional reform.
axes.counterEvidence: Representative judgment tempers plebiscitary mechanisms; respect for institutions does not mean executive immunity.

answers.rationale: Regular elections renew parliamentary legitimacy.
Expert panels cannot replace democratic representation.
Modern One Nation citizenship includes universal adult suffrage.
A prime minister remains answerable to parliament.
Legitimate opposition sustains constitutional continuity.
Financial scrutiny protects responsible administration.
Independent courts enforce established constitutional limits.
Union appointment would exclude other citizens.
The governing party cannot police electoral opinion.
Referendums can settle major issues but bypass deliberative representation.
Cabinet, parliament and courts constrain individual leadership.
Defined removal preserves institutions against personal abuse.
Political convenience cannot authorise cancelling accountability.
Recall deters misconduct but can destabilise representative judgment.
Government requires constitutional and electoral accountability.
Military intervention would destroy civilian parliamentary continuity.

axes.brief: Freedom is situated within lawful order, responsibility and community.
axes.counterEvidence: Generous social policy qualifies punitive moralism; judicial safeguards constrain public-order powers.

answers.rationale: Personal freedom and responsibility for dependency pull differently.
Judicially approved investigation fits lawful public protection.
Peaceful protest matters, but access and public order also matter.
Institutional criticism remains part of constitutional freedom.
Proportionate health protection must respect adult judgment.
Routine long-term tracking is excessive without concrete need.
Road safety justifies modest preventive checks.
A court finding supplies restraint against a serious risk.
Adult choice deserves tolerance despite moral disagreement.
Routine communication need not require state identification.
Serious threats may justify searches only with tightly bounded powers.
Evidence of serious disorder can justify preventive limits.
Home searches normally need independent legal authorisation.
Accountability and legitimate confidentiality require public-interest balancing.
Public safety outweighs a general private-arms presumption.
Indefinite detention without courts abandons the rule of law.

axes.brief: TRG's open-minded social policy combines common belonging with accommodation.
axes.counterEvidence: A shared civic community does not require either cultural uniformity or unconditional group precedence.

answers.rationale: Common institutions and minority practices deserve contextual reconciliation.
Reasonable accommodation strengthens inclusive civic membership.
Some integration is expected without wholesale cultural assimilation.
Distinct heritage can coexist with national belonging.
A common service language is practical, with access exceptions.
Acknowledging Indigenous peoples can strengthen shared national history.
Inherited traditions deserve support alongside minority participation.
Community demands should not automatically override shared obligations.
A common calendar and practical accommodation can coexist.
National identity can incorporate several inherited communities.
Participation in wider civic life sustains social cohesion.
Additional signage is useful where need justifies cost.
National solidarity need not suppress family community attachments.
Religious accommodation depends on the reason for general clothing restrictions.
Plural cultural lives can share constitutional commitments.
Integration requires shared participation while allowing distinct customs.

axes.brief: Social cohesion supports managed migration, humanitarian protection and family stability.
axes.counterEvidence: An open-minded tradition is not synonymous with unlimited admission; resource pressures require management.

answers.rationale: Planned intake should reflect housing and employment capacity.
Opportunity to migrate is legitimate but not unconditional.
Family and refugee claims qualify skills selection.
Stable families strengthen the community into which migrants settle.
Humanitarian need warrants exceptions to economic selection.
Regularisation needs exceptional grounds rather than a general entitlement.
Public capacity can outweigh additional employer demand.
Service pressures justify moderation while supply expands.
Planning totals and family unity need balancing.
Genuine employment supports controlled migration.
Sponsorship helps integration but cannot cover every protection case.

Local education and established ties favour a graduate route, while capacity-sensitive admission may require an employment or family basis. The conditional balance concerns eligibility for a route, not automatic residence.
Persecution can justify protection beyond ordinary intake plans.
Integration prospects should not become crude cultural-origin discrimination.
Lawfully settled residents should receive fair basic social protection.
Plurality is welcome, but admissions serve broader social purposes.

axes.brief: Internationalist conservatism favours alliances, diplomacy and credible defence.
axes.counterEvidence: Prudence rejects both automatic intervention and abandonment of collective defence.

answers.rationale: Exceptional force may be justified, but interests alone are insufficient.
Diplomacy normally precedes costly armed action.
Credible deterrence warrants substantial but proportionate expenditure.
Imminent attack can warrant necessary defensive action.
Defence is central, though lawful exceptional interventions remain possible.
Civic duty supports service while professional effectiveness weighs against compulsion.
Prudent concessions can prevent disproportionate military costs.
Reliability and human responsibility must qualify weapons efficiency.
Defence should outweigh ambitious military transformation abroad.
Allied commitments exclude pacifism at every cost.
Alliances can require sustainable expeditionary capability.
Negotiation is preferable to starting territorial wars.
Deterrent threats may work but carry serious escalation risks.
Avoiding unnecessary war is a central prudential concern.
Responsible intelligence supports deterrence despite diplomatic friction.
Verifiable mutual arms limits can preserve security.

axes.brief: TRG explicitly supports internationalism and the ECHR alongside national parliamentary institutions.
axes.counterEvidence: Treaty cooperation does not automatically entail world federation or a shared currency.

answers.rationale: National sovereignty operates through agreed international obligations.
Institutions voluntarily joined can deliver binding decisions.
International judgments should be honoured within valid commitments.
Alliances provide continuity and shared security.
Exit requires lawful procedures and respect for partners.
Agreed international review reinforces rights and accountability.
National interests and common obligations require prudent balancing.
Cross-border environmental issues justify shared institutions.
Common foreign-policy cooperation need not threaten national identity.
TRG's ECHR commitment supports external rights obligations.
Currency sharing is an institutional choice, not a universal principle.
Pooling capacity helps solve problems beyond individual states.
Cooperation is possible while democratic responsibility for borders remains.
Negotiated common trade rules support international stability.
Federation depends on consent and preservation of effective accountability.
Reliable common rules can outweigh immediate tactical advantage.

axes.brief: One Nation combines enterprise, social provision and pragmatic ownership.
axes.counterEvidence: TRG helped advance Right to Buy; social concern does not entail blanket nationalisation.

answers.rationale: Private enterprise supplies much ordinary economic activity.
Network monopolies can warrant accountable public ownership.
Practical results matter more than categorical ownership preference.
Public enterprise needs a demonstrated social purpose.
A substantial public healthcare sector supports shared security.
Rail infrastructure has coordination and public-service characteristics.
Comparable access at lower cost can justify contracting.
A public bank is useful only with a clear public function.
Sales should be judged individually rather than ideologically.
Social housing remains important alongside property ownership.
Effective security regulation can make nationalisation unnecessary.
Resource ownership depends on public value and institutional performance.
Service quality and accountability decide routine outsourcing.
Strategic capacity can outweigh immediate receipts.
Restructuring, public value and sale options all need assessment.
A public broadcaster can sustain shared civic institutions.

axes.brief: Pragmatic internationalism generally favours trade while protecting exceptional strategic capacity.
axes.counterEvidence: Gradual adaptation and social cohesion qualify wholesale exposure to disruptive competition.

answers.rationale: Permanent protective tariffs risk burdening the wider community.
Openness is desirable with help for affected communities.
Domestic resilience can matter alongside procurement value.
Businesses normally choose efficient international suppliers.
Essential capacity can justify limited strategic safeguards.
Unilateral reductions depend on negotiating and domestic circumstances.
Temporary support requires a credible path to competitiveness.
Foreign investment is welcome within ordinary public safeguards.
Food resilience and consumer costs deserve balancing.
Adaptation is preferable to indefinite producer shelter.
Proportionate retaliation may support negotiation but can escalate losses.
Origin-neutral taxes generally protect fair competition.
Demonstrable foreign subsidy distortion can warrant proportionate remedies.
Agreements should open trade while managing essential dependencies.
Sensitive national assets can justify ownership screening.
Ordinary online services should generally trade freely.

axes.brief: Markets are useful within a mixed economy and social responsibilities.
axes.counterEvidence: One Nation intervention should correct specific problems rather than impose a comprehensive command system.

answers.rationale: Ordinary enterprise should retain operational discretion.
Mandatory output schedules are usually too rigid.
Market prices are useful with protection against exploitation.
Strategic investment can address neglected public needs.
Demand matters, but abrupt closure can harm whole communities.
Affordability measures must avoid damaging supply.
New entrants should normally face fair open competition.
Directed credit needs safeguards against political favouritism.
Capital freedom is legitimate subject to systemic stability.
Targeted support can preserve strategically valuable regional employment.
Currency experimentation must not jeopardise financial confidence.
A reasonable wage floor reconciles enterprise with social duty.
Negotiation remains preferable to pervasive national wage schedules.
Macroeconomic coordination must balance stability and elected priorities.
Rental affordability and supply call for pragmatic regulation.
Ordinary production should not be comprehensively administered.

axes.brief: Social obligation supports adequate benefits and progressive contributions while preserving incentives.
axes.counterEvidence: Compassionate conservatism aims at cohesion rather than equality of every outcome.

answers.rationale: Moderate redistribution can prevent divisive deprivation.
Inequality matters where it weakens cohesion, not as an absolute evil.
An adequate social floor can justify additional revenue.
Basic protection and broader participation must be reconciled.
Progressive taxation reflects differing capacities to contribute.
Enterprise incentives must be weighed against shared social duties.
Inheritance policy balances family continuity and fair opportunity.
Continuing hardship needs more than a mechanical deadline.
Wealth taxation requires scrutiny of fairness and practical consequences.
Benefits cannot be set solely by contributors' preferences.
Social membership includes participation beyond physical subsistence.
Tax cuts and benefit increases depend on actual social conditions.
In-work support can reinforce responsibility and employment.
Equal marginal rates are not required for reasonable incentives.
Land reform needs a concrete injustice and proportionate remedy.
Support can legitimately prevent exclusion before destitution occurs.

axes.brief: Civil government coexists with inherited religious institutions and freedom of conscience.
axes.counterEvidence: Respect for an established church does not entail clerical control of all public law.

answers.rationale: Policy should offer public reasons beyond denominational teaching.
Religious insight can inform debate without becoming binding law.
Parliamentary government requires no general clerical approval.
Historic recognition and equal citizenship can coexist conditionally.
Public teaching should inform rather than compel belief.
Faith formation belongs primarily to voluntary families and communities.
Enforceable law ultimately comes from civil institutions.
Advisory historical roles differ from a religious veto.
Traditional worship may remain in inclusive state ceremonies.
Heritage and community support differ from subsidising conversion.
Inherited symbols can be tolerated without exclusive citizenship.
Longstanding religious festivals form part of national continuity.
Reforming historic clerical seats requires balancing inheritance and representation.
Community contributions may justify exemptions, but religion alone is contested.
Civil marriage should remain accessible without religious authorisation.
Voluntary arbitration is possible only under civil-rights safeguards.

axes.brief: Moderate conservatism supports gradual adaptation and generous social policy.
axes.counterEvidence: TRG's liberal conservatism should not be equated with rigid restoration of every historical norm.

answers.rationale: Institutions can adapt while retaining social continuity.
Tradition matters but cannot automatically defeat justified reform.
Different households deserve dignity and practical inclusion.
Rigid roles conflict with open-minded equal opportunity.
Equal marriage can become part of the settled constitutional order.
Stable two-parent families may be encouraged without excluding others.
Early abortion involves competing autonomy and moral considerations.
Parents' responsibilities coexist with children's educational interests.
Stable caregiving should be assessed without categorical exclusion.
Modesty remains a social preference rather than universal obligation.
Respect for identity and familiar language should accommodate each other.
Moral continuity has value while customs remain open to correction.
Individual choices outside traditional roles deserve social tolerance.
Gradual reform preserves trust and tests consequences.
Age-appropriate understanding and family participation both matter.
Historical connection can have value beyond immediate utility.

axes.brief: Prudence favours incremental innovation, environmental stewardship and assessment of unintended consequences.
axes.counterEvidence: Conservatism permits useful change; cautious adoption is not technological prohibition.

answers.rationale: Benefits warrant adoption when risk controls are credible.
Pilots help reveal consequences before universal deployment.
Public gains and permanent habitat loss require careful comparison.
Medical safety should precede widespread exposure.
Productivity matters alongside community disruption and retraining capacity.
Preservation is valuable but essential infrastructure can outweigh it.
Food innovation requires convincing practical and ecological assessment.
Irreversible enhancement needs strong long-term safety grounds.
Technological optimism cannot replace conservation or practical evidence.
Investigating poorly understood effects is ordinary prudent government.
Basic safety may be insufficient for lasting invasive enhancement.
Reliable diagnosis requires evidence across the actual patient population.
Heritable enhancement risks justify stronger restraint than therapeutic research.
Ecological persistence warrants evidence beyond initial crop yields.
Housing needs and landscape continuity both have legitimate weight.
Irreversible harm calls for a particularly demanding threshold.

axes.brief: Local communities deserve practical autonomy within a coherent national settlement.
axes.counterEvidence: One Nation solidarity also requires common services and resources across regions.

answers.rationale: Regional self-government preserves meaningful local responsibility.
Constitutional allocation should govern disputes, not either level's preference.
A single vote may not settle obligations and minority protections.
National guarantees may justify intervention, but local mandates matter.
Regional institutional variation is legitimate within common rights.
Locally rooted policing should retain accountability to communities.
Fiscal autonomy must coexist with support for poorer areas.
National educational essentials can coexist with regional variation.
Local tax choices connect responsibility with expenditure.
Common labour floors protect cohesion across the country.
Local preference matters alongside wider administrative consequences.
Shared healthcare guarantees express national social obligation.
Local Indigenous institutions can fit a plural constitutional settlement.
Some limits may protect solidarity without eliminating local competition.
Local effects are generally best handled locally.
A multi-region crisis requires coherent coordination.

axes.brief: Conservative socialisation and human imperfection are compatible with interaction between biology and upbringing.
axes.counterEvidence: Tradition is not evidence for hereditary race differences. Trait-specific neutral answers explicitly reflect a mixed model.

answers.rationale: Family and community institutions cultivate behaviour.

International IQ comparisons involve education, health, measurement and inheritance; the scoped doctrine does not assign a stable causal priority. This representative response adopts a mixed model rather than inferring biology from citizenship or tradition.
Sex differences can reflect both social roles and biology.
Stress sensitivity combines predisposition with experience.
Opportunities and community practices shape interests.
Prudence treats risk behaviour as learned and dispositional.
Cooperation is cultivated through stable associations.
Empathy depends on human capacities and social cultivation.
Attention cannot be assigned one dominant cause from conservative principles.
Moral intuitions are substantially transmitted through custom and upbringing.
Historical experience informs what communities perceive as danger.
Temperament includes disposition and formation without a universal ranking.
Attraction reflects embodied preferences and changing conventions.

Violence rates can reflect social conditions, institutions and individual dispositions; the doctrine supplies no defensible racial causal ranking. The representative model therefore withholds primacy rather than deriving empirical claims from equal rights.
Moral habits are cultivated rather than assigned by racial descent.
Unequal opportunity and social expectations can influence pay.

review.reviewer: Codex independent assessment reviewer /root/socialist_green (separate from author)
review.notes: Independently read all 240 answers against the current bank and checked the scoped primary doctrine plus scholarship/context. No scores or desired locations were consulted. Reviewed literal government authority, ownership versus funding, official religious review versus veto, graduate routes versus guaranteed residence, military initiation versus response, and causal claims versus moral equality. Corrections: restricted-immigration-open-immigration-12: 1 -> 0. The inferred modern-policy answers and mixed causal models remain representative applications, not documented answers by every adherent or scientific causal estimates. Similarity review is a subsequent mechanical check. Validation returned zero errors. Explicitly examined neutral-count warnings: authority-liberty 5/16, assimilation-multiculturalism 8/16, restricted-immigration-open-immigration 5/16, nationalism-internationalism 6/16, public-private 7/16, protectionism-free-trade 5/16, planning-free-market 7/16, high-redistribution-low-redistribution 7/16, secular-religious 7/16, progressive-traditionalist 6/16, innovation-caution 7/16, central-local 6/16, culture-nature 9/16. Retained condition-dependent policy tradeoffs and representative interaction models; in particular the Culture vs Nature neutrals withhold causal primacy rather than converting equal rights into empirical proof. High neutrality records weaker doctrinal determination and must not be presented as a precisely measured consensus among adherents. No answers were changed after inspecting validation scores.
